title: The next experiments
evidenceStatus: Frozen authored roadmap: eight benchmark cards and twelve product ideas; nineteen Proposed, one Implemented; no model decisions on this route
summary: The atlas clearly distinguishes proposals from results and links the completed Typed Decisions study. It lacks structured split, revision, scorer, coverage and budget fields, so its prose cannot establish whether a future run is complete. A versioned study planner would make the shortlist executable without implying unrun evidence.
strengths: All twenty cards state a question, demo, protocol, measure and caveat.
Nineteen Proposed entries and one Implemented entry match the explicit UI warning and actual local-model link.
Caveats correctly separate intent/slots, retrieval/verification, structured state/pixels and model decisions/audio generation.

findings.title: Coverage cannot be derived from prose
findings.evidence: research.ts:2 and :111; probes/benchmark-atlas.json finds zero structured IDs, revisions, splits, expected counts, scorers, budgets or evidence paths across twenty entries; only BoolQ and Typed Decisions state explicit evaluation counts.
findings.impact: A sampled pilot could be promoted to Implemented without a machine-checkable completeness criterion.
findings.fix: Define a typed run manifest with exact IDs, split/revision/scorer hashes, expected/completed coverage and artifact-derived status; separate UI implementation from benchmark completion.

findings.title: Version and access assumptions remain implicit
findings.evidence: research.ts:59 says 51 MASSIVE languages without a version; official 1.1 adds Catalan for 52. WildGuardMix requires accepted access conditions; SciFact test labels are not public in its documented workflow.
findings.impact: Counts and execution feasibility change with the chosen release and access/scoring route.
findings.fix: Record source revision, verified date, precise split, access method and explicit setup blockers before scheduling.

findings.title: Proxy metrics can change the benchmark task
findings.evidence: research.ts:47 describes SciFact label/evidence metrics without official abstract/rationale scoring variants. :87 describes AgentDojo paired execution but lacks a pinned task/attack matrix.
findings.impact: Gold-evidence classification or hostile-snippet labeling could be mistaken for full retrieval/agent outcomes; expanded dataset rows can inflate independent case counts.
findings.fix: Declare unit of evaluation, model-visible fields, official scorer and assisted variants; preserve unique claim/task IDs and actual end-task outcomes.

findings.title: The UI gives no readiness or budget comparison
findings.evidence: local-models.tsx:573 and :621 offer only tab/category filters and uniform cards; no effort, dependency, request-volume or next-deliverable fields.
findings.impact: A 3270-case binary run looks as ready as a 151674-case multilingual run or a multi-turn agent study.
findings.fix: Add a selectable study tray with count/budget arithmetic, prerequisites, evidence gaps and a concrete next artifact.

simulation.title: A study planner with inspectable evidence
simulation.description: Select a benchmark and controllers, inspect source/scorer/coverage, compare a pilot with the full run, export an immutable manifest and open a coverage ledger for recorded evidence.
simulation.jevsRole: Answer benchmark questions only during a separate explicit run. A planning suggestion must never supply authoritative counts or scores.
simulation.codeRole: Own dataset metadata, revisions, exact IDs, budget arithmetic, job states, request fingerprints, resumable evidence and scoring.
acceptanceCriteria: A 100-case pilot cannot display full coverage.
Wrong revisions, duplicates or missing IDs fail publication.
Interrupted runs resume to the same declared set without losing failures or duplicating completed decisions.
Displayed totals equal the exported manifest and labels/reasons never enter model input.
Keyboard users can inspect provenance and coverage; study selection survives filter changes.

evaluation.design: Validate all twenty roadmap entries and evidence links before any benchmark calls. First full classifier tranche: BoolQ dev3270, ANLI test3200 across rounds, PAWS-Wiki Final test8000, totaling14470 cases per policy. Three hosted repeats need43410 logical decisions and2172 verified twenty-case batches before retries. Pin IDs/scorers, keep calibration on development data, report paired clustered intervals and preserve failures. Advanced studies require their own manifests and end-task checks.
baselines: Appropriate frozen local classifier and Jev under identical visible evidence
No-defense and code-filter acting-agent baselines for AgentDojo
metrics: Accuracy with exact numerator/denominator; per-round/language/task metrics
Calibration and selective risk on held-out cases
Official SciFact evidence/label scoring and actual AgentDojo clean utility/attack success
Physical requests, logical decisions, failures, retries, wall time and cost

coverage.current: Seven benchmark proposals have zero predictions here. One implemented card links all400 Typed Decisions test cases/2000 decisions per model. Twelve product ideas are also proposals.
coverage.full: BoolQ3270 labeled dev; ANLI3200 test; PAWS-Wiki8000 test; SciFact300 unique labeled dev plus300 unlabeled test; MASSIVE1.0 151674 or1.1 154648 test utterances; WildGuardTest1725 items with up to5175 labels; original AgentDojo97 tasks/629 security cases, current pinned matrix must be enumerated; Typed Decisions400 cases already complete.
coverage.feasibility: Bounded classifiers are practical with resumable batches. MASSIVE requires a larger declared budget. WildGuard access and SciFact test scoring are setup blockers. AgentDojo requires sandboxed multi-turn execution and separate acting-model/Jev request counts. No proposed benchmark was run.
